newsitem.title: USA: North Carolina approves $2.75 bln school, road GOs.
newsitem.headline: North Carolina approves $2.75 bln school, road GOs.

text.p: North Carolina voters approved a $1.8 billion general obligation bond issue for schools and a $950 million GO bond issue for roads, officials at the state treausurer's office said Wednesday.
Final vote tallies were unavailable, but Raleigh News and Observer reported that with 62 percent of the precincts counted, the school bond issue led by a margin of nearly 3-1.
School bond proceeds will be divided among the state's 118 school districts under a matching formula based on student population, population growth rates and ability to pay.
Most of the road bond money will be used to speed construction of loop roads around seven urban areas.
Debt service on the school bonds is to be repaid with general revenues, while the road bonds are backed with revenues from the state's highway trust fund.
